correctness.rationale: For each strictly positive g, gamma, and r, the completely positive reset resolvent gives a unique stationary state. Exact scalar stationarity equations yield the full X-state, and the Wootters concurrence formula gives an iff quadratic entanglement threshold. The coupling derivative has a unique positive root within the entangled interval, proving the global optimizer; a one-variable monotonicity argument proves the sharp envelope and limiting bounds. Independent full Liouvillian solves at 85 parameter triples and further checks total 782 assertions. Finite checks supplement, not replace, the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The candidate gives the complete sharp phase boundary and coupling-optimized concurrence for joint Poisson ground re-preparation in a nonunital, spontaneously emitting pair-conversion model. Full primary text shows that the related closed-reset and locally reset dissipative models do not state this generator or envelope. Two highly similar published mathematical results use pure local dephasing or unital bit-flip noise; neither has dissipative transfers from the doubly excited state to both singly excited populations. The mathematics cannot be recovered by renaming rates or taking a direct corollary. Unindexed general open-system solutions remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed two-qubit master-equation paper may already solve the identical joint-reset, spontaneous-emission, coherent-pair-drive generator in equivalent XX notation.
The no-reset limit and qualitative reset assistance have old antecedents; no novelty is asserted for those standalone facts.
Publication-priority comparisons cannot certify global uniqueness even after semantic searches and relevant primary full-text inspection.

value.rationale: The pair-pumped emitter system is motivated by stationary entanglement generation under inevitable local spontaneous emission. The exact threshold classifies when collective re-preparation rescues entanglement otherwise absent; the unique global coupling optimum and strictly increasing reset-optimized envelope reveal a nontrivial control tradeoff and quantitative upper bound. It is a natural complete phase classification, not a substitution in a preexisting dephasing/bit-flip result, and does not require a downstream general theorem to be useful.
